question: Do explicit neural charge and class penalties alter alpha/gamma recovery when blind candidates, onsets, templates, initialization and whitening are held fixed?
data_role: 20 disclosed development windows; no fresh final test

fixed_settings.onsets: fixed blind union; no truth input
fixed_settings.count: fixed union size; q>=500 report selection may differ
fixed_settings.shape_charge: initial candidate charge, common to all arms
fixed_settings.whitening: same cached physical baseline, fixed AR(1)

score_definition: Q>=500 pe; emission [5,15) us; time-only matching<=10ns, correct class and |dQ/Q|<=20%

bootstrap.unit: paired whole windows stratified by two gamma backgrounds and two alpha injection rates

environment.runtime: Project GAGG Python; existing NumPy/SciPy; no Torch needed for cached-output ablation

evidence: Reuses project L28/L29, existing Kim2023/Morad2024 notes; penalty separation is a project diagnostic, not a paper reproduction
limits: Only explicit penalty effects at fixed candidates/onsets; production timing/additions differ
None still uses common neural candidates and initial shape charges
Development sample and limited gamma counts; no real-detector/energy-calibrated performance claim
